option_description: Indicates whether Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) Route Origin Validation (ROV) is enforced with an 'invalid-reject' policy on border routers and upstream transit providers serving the repository infrastructure, ensuring that BGP route announcements for repository IP space are cryptographically verified and invalid routes are dropped.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'bgp_route_hijack_redirecting_git_traffic' when rpki_validation_enforced is false, regardless of the transport protocol in use. Without RPKI, an autonomous-system-level adversary can hijack BGP route announcements for repository IP prefixes, transparently redirecting all git clone and push traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure. For plaintext protocols this immediately exposes all data; for TLS protocols the attacker can attempt certificate impersonation or traffic analysis.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use an online RPKI validation service to check whether the IP prefixes hosting the repository infrastructure have valid ROAs (Route Origin Authorizations) and whether the hosting provider enforces ROV.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-empty validating_roas array with 'validity: valid' status confirms ROA coverage; check provider's ROV enforcement separately.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Contact the network/infrastructure team or cloud provider to confirm whether RPKI ROV with 'invalid-reject' policy is enforced on all border routers and upstream transit peering sessions serving repository host IP prefixes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written confirmation from network team that RPKI ROV is enforced with invalid-reject (not invalid-warn) policy on all border router BGP sessions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the RPKI validity state of repository host IP prefixes using the Cloudflare or RIPE RPKI validator API.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status 'valid' confirms ROA exists; separately verify that the hosting AS enforces invalid-reject policy through provider documentation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-managed network infrastructure, inspect border router BGP configuration for RPKI ROV policy statements applied to eBGP peer sessions.
how_to_obtain.command: ssh $BORDER_ROUTER 'show bgp rpki servers' && ssh $BORDER_ROUTER 'show route protocol bgp validation-state invalid'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RPKI server entries present with reachable status and zero or minimal invalid routes accepted (invalid-reject policy active).

option_description: Specifies the transport protocol used for all git clone, fetch, and push operations to the repository host. 'https' and 'ssh' provide encrypted transports; 'http' and 'git' are plaintext protocols that transmit all repository data and credentials without encryption.
security_impact: The Rego policy evaluates git_transport_protocol in two contexts: 'bgp_route_hijack_redirecting_git_traffic' is triggered unconditionally when the protocol is 'http' or 'git' (plaintext provides no protection against route hijack interception), and it is also triggered for 'https' or 'ssh' when tls_certificate_pinning_enabled is false (encrypted transport alone does not prevent impersonation at a hijacked endpoint). Additionally, 'plaintext_git_protocol_exposure' fires when 'git' or 'http' appears in configured remote protocols.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect all configured git remote URLs across developer workstations and CI/CD pipeline configurations to enumerate which protocols are in use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote URLs prefixed with 'https://' or 'git@' (SSH) are secure; URLs prefixed with 'git://' or 'http://' indicate insecure plaintext transport.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search CI/CD pipeline configuration files for git remote URLs to identify any plaintext protocol usage in automated build contexts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches for 'git://' or 'http://' prefixed repository URLs; all URLs should use 'https://' or 'git@' (SSH) format.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the repository platform, check the repository clone URL widget to see which protocols are offered and whether plaintext options (git:// or http://) are presented as defaults or available options.
how_to_obtain.navigation: GitHub: Repository main page > Code button > Clone options (HTTPS/SSH/GitHub CLI) | GitLab: Repository main page > Clone dropdown
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only HTTPS and SSH clone URLs are presented; absence of a 'git://' URL option indicates plaintext protocol is not offered by the platform.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted git infrastructure (Gitea, GitLab), check server-level protocol enablement configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration shows only 'https' or 'ssh' protocols enabled; absence of git:// listener confirms plaintext protocol is blocked.

option_description: Indicates whether git client tooling (on developer workstations and CI/CD runners) is configured with TLS certificate pinning via http.pinnedPubkey, a custom CA bundle via http.sslCAInfo, or equivalent strict certificate validation settings that prevent acceptance of arbitrary certificates presented by a rogue endpoint.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'bgp_route_hijack_redirecting_git_traffic' when rpki_validation_enforced is false AND the transport protocol is 'https' or 'ssh' but tls_certificate_pinning_enabled is false. Without pinning, a BGP hijack adversary can serve a fraudulently obtained or self-signed TLS certificate for the repository hostname, and git clients using only standard CA validation may accept it if the attacker controls a trusted CA or performs a CA compromise, allowing transparent interception of encrypted git traffic.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect global and repository-level git configuration files for certificate pinning or custom CA settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of 'http.pinnedPubkey' with a sha256// hash value confirms pinning is active; 'http.sslCAInfo' pointing to a custom CA bundle indicates strict CA validation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check CI/CD runner environment configuration and pipeline scripts for git SSL configuration environment variables or git config overrides.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of GIT_SSL_CAINFO pointing to a custom CA or http.pinnedPubkey configured confirms pinning; GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=true is a critical misconfiguration that disables all validation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test whether the git client accepts a certificate from an unexpected CA by simulating a TLS interception (in a lab environment) and observing if the git operation fails with a certificate validation error.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Certificate validation failure error when presented with an untrusted CA confirms strict validation is active; successful connection indicates pinning is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review developer workstation hardening standards and CI/CD platform configuration management (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) to confirm whether git certificate pinning policy is centrally mandated and deployed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration management code enforcing http.pinnedPubkey or a custom sslCAInfo for git operations on all managed workstations and runners.
